requirement_dispositions.note: Bounded, exact, fail-closed containment and cleanup.  This closure changes only the truthfulness of alias discharge, the combined capacity gate for a reservation-less insertion, and the coverage of the declared mutation boundary over probe creation.

Durable, non-contradictory evidence.  A drain row can no longer claim a discharge its canonical result does not prove, and the current artifacts can no longer claim a physical verification and a pending operator hand-off at once.

supersedes_prior_current_report.no_second_snapshot_file: The M2-M36 model keeps exactly one current validation report.  The fourth-repair snapshot exists as a file because its bytes were otherwise unreachable; these bytes are reachable from git and from the immutable closure report, so no second snapshot file is created.
supersedes_prior_current_report.preserved_in: the git object at the starting commit, and -- in full -- in the immutable implementation/M2_ALIAS_CAPACITY_ARTIFACT_TCB_CLOSURE_REPORT.json, which carries every claim the superseded report made, including the full-transcript claim M2-M64 withdraws
supersedes_prior_current_report.reason: The superseded report was the current artifact for the alias-truth / combined-capacity / artifact-coherence / mutation-TCB closure.  Its independent audit refused final closure with M2-B63 and M2-M64, and M2-M64 is a defect of that report itself: it declared 173972 transcript bytes and a SHA-256 over them beside a 29-byte summary that was the only transcript value present.  Its terminal verdict, its counts and its transcript claim therefore describe a superseded revision and are not current.

supersedes_validation_report.model: Option A -- versioned historical snapshot.  The superseded bytes are preserved under a clearly historical filename and the canonical filename carries the single current report, so a third party never has to decide which of two files is authoritative.
supersedes_validation_report.reason: M2-M36.  The superseded report carried the fourth-repair terminal refusal, a limitation declaring M2-B25 implemented but not physically qualified, cgroup delegation recorded as unavailable, and real delegated qualification recorded as false -- alongside two B25 closure objects recording a 125-test delegated run that had in fact succeeded.  One current artifact therefore asserted a physical qualification and its absence.  The bytes are preserved unchanged under the historical filename and this file is the sole current report.
